OK, we have to be careful with the conclusion guys. Here is a link to the actual study. http://ajph.aphapublications.org/doi/pdf/10.2105/AJPH.2015.302773

This is a population-based cohort study using electronic health records from family physicians in the UK. It means they take a large sample of random people who had BMI entries in their medical charts over a certain time. The only individuals excluded were those who underwent bariatric surgery and those who had less than 3 BMI records.

These people were NOT on any specific weight loss plan. Some may have received counselling. Some might have attempted to loose weight and others not. I am sure that if we did a study following motivated hams who actually cut out crap from their diet (especially wheat and sugar) coupled with an active life style (to increase muscle mass and burn calories), the results would have been different.
They make it sound like weight loss is a lottery.
Maybe I am just a little Luddite, but why do people want an app for voat/facebook/other web sites when the browser pulls it up fine?
Why use an app versus a browser?

Simply put, apps are made to be used on devices while web browser versions are meant to be used on a desktop computer. If you use voat on a phone you'll have to scroll from side to side to view the entire screen because our screens are smaller and if you were to use it on an app everything will be made to be viewed on your device without the minor annoyances.

web browser versions are meant to be used on a desktop computer

Not true at all. Websites can be tailored specifically for mobile devices of any size.

If you use Voat on a phone it scales to your screen (for most screens). It definitely needs more work and polish, but there should be no side-to-side scrolling.

Yes but when you use a browser instead of an app you are (caches aside) downloading a lot more data. With an app you can just make a request to the API and parse out the returned JSON object or XML or whatever, but with a browser you are getting the data AND all the information necessary to render it on the browser (html, css, javascript).

On mobile devices this can make a big difference on battery life and performance.

Edit: Unless the browser site runs something like angularjs, but mobile browsers are less efficient at rendering than native apps.

Completely agreed; of course native apps are generally more efficient.

I was disagreeing with the notion that websites are only meant for desktop computers. Strange… I’ve been using the web on mobile devices for more than a decade.

Well all the assets that are downloaded during a given web request come at the cost of bandwidth which can add to your bill if you have limited bandwidth. You are also capped to the experience the web developers provide you. If you have JavaScript disabled or if the site is not accessible enough for you then are stuck. An app can use an API which usually only send back compressed text known as JSON. JSON comes at a small cost to bandwidth and all other assets may be loaded from the app. The app developer can provide a different experience than the site developers, which may have multiple benefits such as improved accessibility, lazy loading of additional content while scrolling, configurable preferences, integration with device camera for easy sharing in the community, etc.

Alerts! If you're using a mobile web browser (yes, Voat has one of the best around), you have to be continually moving to know if you've got mail. In a proper app you'll know when something is coming your way, even if the phone is in your pocket, and a good one will tell you when something interesting is happening in your favorite sub.

Certain functions will be quicker in an app, for example finding Facebook contacts.

Background activity. A computer web browser will keep track of your tabs even when they're not focused. The mobile browser will forget its own ass if you look at a website in another tab or switch to a different app for a few minutes. Come back to the site and go for a slow refresh. OR: post a comment, go kill some zombies (or whatever game the kids are playing these days), snap a chat, whatever, then ping! "Oh I have a reply, lets check that out."
